name: Bell Laboratories quartz clock report
description: A Bell Laboratories quartz-referenced clock was described by J. W. Horton and W. A. Marrison.

impact.note: First clock of a new, more exact kind, used by standards laboratories and observatories; quartz time and frequency standards grew from it. Later watches not counted in reach.

date.basis: Source-reported date for this scoped event.

events.statement: Horton and Marrison presented a report describing a clock referenced to a quartz crystal.

evidence.supports: Reports the October 1927 presentation and the quartz-clock frequency.
Attributes the presentation to Horton and Marrison.
Attributes the presentation to Horton and Marrison.
Identifies the Bell Laboratories quartz-clock engineer as Warren Marrison.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented event for this scoped record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

research.note: Independent parent inspected the cited publisher, museum, BIPM or NIST/PTB passages. Dates retain their event scope; no global priority is inferred.

places.note: Bell Telephone Laboratories; city is the laboratory location rather than an asserted presentation venue.

measures.quantity: Quartz oscillator nominal frequency in the reported clock
measures.subject: Horton and Marrison quartz clock described in the 1927 report

evidence.supports: Reports the quartz clock referenced to a 50 kHz crystal.

caveats: The 1927 report is cited through a later NIST history; later performance figures must not be attributed to the 1927 device.
